rows.speaker: عبدالله بن زمعة
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Zamʿa heard the Prophet rebuke people for laughing at a loud passing wind: why laugh at something you do yourselves?
rows.anchor: عن عبدالله بن زمعة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب ويعظهم في ضحكهم

rows.speaker: بعض علمائنا
rows.claim: Some scholars say laughing at a statement of unbelief can itself make the laugher an unbeliever; some restrict this to cases where the person could control the laughter.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض علمائنا أن من الضحك ما يكفر به الضاحك كالضحك على كلمة كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual progression rule would put the greater before the lesser in a negative statement, since excluding a lesser act does not exclude a greater one.
rows.anchor: الترقي في الإثبات يكون من الأدنى إلى الأعلى وفي النفي على عكس ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: When small and large are a conventional expression for totality, as here, the lesser may precede the greater in a negation.
rows.anchor: كما هنا وقولك ما أعطاني قليلا ولا كثيرا جاز تقديم الأدنى على الأعلى في النفي كما فصله ابن الأثير

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr says the small sins are placed first to draw attention to their importance.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر قدمت الصغيرة اهتماما بها

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl would exclaim that people had been overwhelmed by minor sins before major sins.
rows.anchor: وروى عن الفضيل أنه كان إذا قرأ الآية قال ضجوا والله من الصغائر قبل الكبائر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says people objected to the reckoning they hear described, yet no one complained of injustice; small, disregarded sins accumulate and ruin a person.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة أنه قال في الآية : اشتكى القوم كما تسمعون الاحصاء ولم يشتك أحد ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeds or their recompense are present either written in each person's book or ready before them without delay; the author prefers the latter despite its departure from the apparent wording because it adds a new point.
rows.anchor: واختير المعنى الأخير وإن كان في ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر لأن الكلام عليه تأسيس محض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not exceed the limits He set: He promised reward and its increase, punishment in proportion to guilt, possible forgiveness of sins short of unbelief, and no punishment without an offense.
rows.anchor: لا يتجاوز الحد الذي حده في الثواب والعقاب وإن لم يجب ذلك عليه تعالى عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims agree that God neither punishes someone for an uncommitted deed, reduces earned reward, nor adds punishment beyond the deed; they differ whether this impossibility is revealed or rational.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما أجمع عليه المسلمون وإن اختلفوا في أن امتناع وقوع ما نفي هل هو سمعي أو عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl al-Sunna regard the impossibility as established by revelation, while the Muʿtazila regard it as rational.
rows.anchor: فذهب إلى الأول أهل السنة وإلى الثاني المعتزلة

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī says the denial of injustice is literal; there is no need to say that an act unjust from a human would not be unjust from God because He owns creation.
rows.anchor: قال الخفاجي : الظاهر أنها حقيقة وعليه لا حاجة إلى أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies the popular Sunni position as affirming that no form of injustice is conceivable of God, who acts freely in His dominion.
rows.anchor: لأنه جل شأنه مالك الملك متصرف في ملكه كيف يشاء فلا يتصور في شأنه تعالى شأنه ظلم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's general wording supports the sound view that children of polytheists are not punished, a conclusion supported by reports cited earlier.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعموم الآية على أن أطفال المشركين لا يعذبون وهو القول المنصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command was addressed to all the angels, as the apparent wording indicates.
rows.anchor: كلهم كما هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: بعض الصوفية
rows.claim: Some Sufis exempt the absorbed angels from the command to prostrate.
rows.anchor: واستثنى بعض الصوفية الملائكة المهيمين

rows.speaker: بعض آخر
rows.claim: Another group says only the angels of earth were commanded, not the angels of heaven.
rows.anchor: وبعض آخر ملائكة السماء مطلقا وزعم أن المقول له ملائكة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration to Adam is explained either as a greeting and honor, or as prostrating toward him as the qibla while worshipping God.
rows.anchor: سجود تحية وإكرام أو اسجدوا لجهته على معنى اتخذوه قبله لسجودكم لله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ treats the phrase that Iblis was of the jinn as a circumstantial clause with an implied qad; the author prefers an independent explanatory sentence.
rows.anchor: حال من المستثنى وقد مقدرة والرابط الضمير وهو اختيار أبي البقاء والأول ألصق بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent clause explains why Iblis did not prostrate: he was originally a jinni, not an angel, although he was among the angels and counted with them.
rows.anchor: وهذا ظاهر في أنه ليس من الملائكة نعم كان معهم ومعدودا في عدادهم

rows.speaker: سعد بن مسعود
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn Masʿūd reports that the angels fought the jinn, captured Iblis as a child, and he worshipped and prostrated with the angels.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن مسعود قال : كانت الملائكة تقاتل الجن فسبى إبليس وكان صغيرا

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab gives a similar account of Iblis being captured and living among the angels.
rows.anchor: وأخرج نحوه عن شهر بن حوشب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan condemns those who say Iblis was an angel, citing the verse's statement that he was of the jinn.
rows.anchor: قاتل الله تعالى أقواما زعموا أن إبليس من الملائكة والله تعالى يقول ( كان من الجن )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says Iblis was never an angel, but the root of the jinn as Adam is the root of humanity; this would mean there were no jinn before him.
rows.anchor: ما كان إبليس من الملائكة طرفة عين وإنه لأصل الجن كما إن آدم عليه السلام أصل الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions the reliability of the claim that no jinn preceded Iblis and considers it more plausible that earlier jinn perished, leaving him as the sole ancestor of later jinn and devils, like Noah among humans.
rows.anchor: وفي القلب من صحته ما فيه وأقرب منه إلى الصحة ما قاله جماعة من أنه كان قبله جن إلا أنهم هلكوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Iblis was an angel and the jinn were a tribe among the angels.
rows.anchor: أخرج هذا ابن جرير وابن المنذر وأبو الشيخ في العظمة والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report makes Iblis a noble angelic leader who kept the gardens and ruled the lowest heaven, seas, and earth; pride arose from his status and was exposed by the prostration command.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن إبليس كان من أشراف الملائكة وأكرمهم قبيلة وكان خازنا على الجنان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda argues that if Iblis were not an angel, he would not have been commanded to prostrate; the author answers that he was in the angels' company and counted among them.
rows.anchor: لو لم يكن من الملائكة لم يؤمر بالسجود وأجيب عن هذا بما أشرنا إليه

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Jubayr calls the jinn a group of angels who continually make jewelry for the people of Paradise until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: الجن في الآية حي من الملائكة لم يزالوا يصوغون حلي أهل الجنة حتى تقوم الساعة

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Jubayr interprets Iblis's being of the jinn to mean he was a keeper of the gardens; the author calls this interpretation strange.
rows.anchor: كان من خزنة الجنان وهو تأويل عجيب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A report from Qatāda glosses jinn as those hidden from obedience to God, deriving the word from concealment; the author says Qatāda is more commonly reported to hold the Ibn ʿAbbās view.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أن معنى كونه من الجن أنه أجن عن طاعة الله تعالى أي ستر ومنع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Iblis was originally an angel and became one of the jinn through metamorphosis.
rows.anchor: صار منهم بالمسخ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account says Iblis was counted among the jinn because he shared their disobedience; some angels had previously rebelled and an angelic force was sent to fight them.
rows.anchor: عد منهم لموافقته إياهم في المعصية حيث أنهم كانوا من قبل عاصين

rows.speaker: التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī says angelic impeccability is disputed and has no decisive proof; some held only messengers and the closest angels infallible, not all angels.
rows.anchor: ولا قاطع في العصمة كما قال العلامة التفتازاني

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reports a group who affirm infallibility for angelic messengers and those nearest God, but not the other angels.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر القاضي عياض أن طائفة ذهبوا إلى عصمة الرسل منهم والمقربين عليهم السلام ولم يقولوا بعصمة غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says claiming Iblis was an angel remains difficult because the verse's wording resists it and reports do not support making him a non-elite angel or an earthly angel exempt from impeccability.
rows.anchor: ويبقى عليه أيضا أن الآية تأبى مدعاه وكذا لو ذهب إلى ما نقل عن بعض الصوفية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains فسق عن أمر ربه as leaving God's obedience, comparing the root to a date escaping its husk and a mouse leaving its hole; the usage motivates عن.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء وأصله من فسق الرطب إذا خرج عن قشره وسموا الفأرة فاسقة لخروجها من جحرها

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba's line is cited as poetic evidence for فسق عن meaning to depart from a course or aim.
rows.anchor: قول رؤبة : يهوين في نجد وغورا غائرا فواسقا عن قصدها جوائرا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says this sense was not found in pre-Islamic poetry or reports and that Arabs used the word after the Qurʾān; al-Mubarrad agrees, though the author says al-Farrāʾ may only be explaining the sense.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : لم نسمع ذلك في شيء من أشعار الجاهلية ولا أحاديثها وإنما تكلم به العرب بعد نزول القرآن

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub takes عن causally: Iblis became sinful because God commanded the angels, among whom he was counted, to prostrate; the author prefers the ordinary sense of leaving obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( عن ) للسببية كما في قولهم كسوته عن عرى وأطعمته عن جوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers فسق عن as departure from God's command; the following ف may connect the sin to Iblis's jinn nature or to his refusal to prostrate.
rows.anchor: والأظهر ما ذكر أولا والفاء سببية

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī says the causal ف that is not a conjunction still carries sequence and can introduce a consequence; the author rejects the objection because causation itself makes the sequence sound.
rows.anchor: قال الرضي : والفاء التي لغير العطف وهي التي تسمى فاء السببية لا تخلو أيضا من معنى الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title Lord underscores the ugliness of Iblis rebelling against the very Lord who commanded him.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية المنافية للفسق لبيان قبح ما فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story warns proud people who boast of lineage and wealth and disdain poor believers that such conduct follows Iblis's prompting.
rows.anchor: لما فيها من تشديد التنكير على المتكبرين المفتخرين بأنسابهم وأموالهم المستنكفين عن الانتظام

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the story to the preceding Judgment scene: Iblis led criminals to sins and the worship of partners, so recalling their enmity warns against his temptations.
rows.anchor: اختار أبو حيان في وجهه أنه سبحانه لما ذكر يوم القيامة والحشر وذكر خوف المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is not redundant with its other Qurʾānic appearances because each occurrence serves a distinct purpose and appears in different styles and wording.
rows.anchor: لا يعد ذكر هذه القصة عنا مع ذكرها قبل تكرارا لأن ذكرها هنا لفائد غير الفائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated Qurʾānic stories differ in style, wording, and expression, and their repetition contains divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: أكثر المكررات ظاهر أمختلفة الأساليب متفاوتة الألفاظ والعبارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses denial and astonishment, while the ف connects the question to the preceding account; the author notes two possible ways to construe that relation.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار والتعجب والفاء للتعقيب والمراد إما إنكار أن يعقب اتخاذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of ذرية is offspring, so the verse indicates that Iblis has children.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد من الذرية الأولاد فتكون الآية دالة على أن له أولادا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that God told Iblis He would create offspring for him alongside every child of Adam, with a devil paired to each human child.
rows.anchor: أنا لا أخلق لآدم ذرية إلا ذرأت لك مثلها فليس يولد لآدم ولد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Iblis copulates and reproduces as human beings do.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة أنه قال : إنه ينكح وينسل كما ينسل بنو آدم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī is reported to infer from the word progeny that Iblis must have a wife, though another report has him say he had never heard of such a wedding.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن الشعبي أنه قال : لا تكون ذرية إلا من زوجة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid names five children of Iblis: Thabr, al-Aʿwar, Dāsim, Masūṭ, and Zalinbūr, assigning them roles in misfortune, agitation, and separating spouses.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي الدنيا في المكائد وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد أنه قال : ولد إبليس خمسة ثبر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another report, Mujāhid assigns adultery to al-Aʿwar, baseless lies to Masūṭ, household entry and eating when God's name is not invoked to Raʾsim, and markets to Zalinbūr.
rows.anchor: وفى روايه أخرى عنه أن الأعور صاحب الزنا ومسوط صاحب أخبار الكذب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account says Iblis laid five eggs which hatched into his five named children; another describes the eggs as emerging from his anus.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الخمسة من خمس بيضات باضها اللعين وقيل إنه عليه اللعنة يدخل ذنبه في دبره فيبيض فتنفلق

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān reports that all of Iblis's progeny came from five eggs and that more than the tribes of Rabīʿa and Muḍar gather against one believer; the author leaves the reports' reliability to God.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سفيان أن جميع ذريته من خمس بيضات باضها قال : وبلغني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some deny that Iblis has children and take progeny figuratively for his followers among the devils.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا ولد له والمراد من الذرية الاتباع من الشياطين وعبر عنه بذلك مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows progeny to mean children, followers, or both together, including a combined literal and figurative sense where that is accepted.
rows.anchor: وقيل ولعله الحق إن له أولادا أو أتباعا ويجوز أن يراد من الذرية مجموعهما معا

rows.speaker: بعض الأخبار
rows.claim: Some reports identify Hāma as an Iblis descendant who believed in Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the Prophet; the author says the birth's mechanics need not be known if the report is sound.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في بعض الأخبار أن ممن ينسب إليه بالولاد من آمن بنوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ونبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: نافي ملكيته
rows.claim: Those who deny that Iblis was an angel argue that the verse gives him progeny, whereas angels do not have offspring.
rows.anchor: واستدل نافي ملكيته بظاهر الآية حيث أفادت أنه له ذرية والملائكة ليس لهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offspring argument does not prove Iblis was never an angel: he could have been transformed after disobedience, and the verse does not say he had children before it.
rows.anchor: بعد أن عصى مسخ وخرج عن الملكية فصار له أولاد ولم تفد الآية أن له أولادا قبل العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من دوني means taking Iblis's family as allies in God's place and substituting their obedience for obedience to God.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال أي أفتتخذونهم أولياء مجاوزين عني إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular enemy describes a plural group collectively, as in the Qurʾānic descriptions of Abraham's false gods and hypocrites as an enemy.
rows.anchor: أي أعداء كما في قوله تعالى ( فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem about a free man forced into friendship with an enemy illustrates the misery of having no alternative to befriending an enemy.
rows.anchor: ومن نكد الدنيا على الحر أن يرى عدوا له ما من صداقته بد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the censure, oppressors are those who put things in the wrong place; إبليس and his progeny are the blameworthy substitute for God, with بئس's subject implicit and بدلا a specification.
rows.anchor: أي بئس البدل من الله تعالى للظالمين إبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to third person and the label wrongdoers signal intense divine displeasure and mark their act as wicked injustice.
rows.anchor: وفي الالتفات إلى الغيبة مع وضع الظالمين موضع ضمير المخاطبين من الإيذان بكمال السخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains why Iblis and his progeny do not deserve to be taken as allies: their corrupt origin, rebellion, and enmity have already disqualified them.
rows.anchor: استئناف مسوق لبيان عدم استحقاق إبليس وذريته للاتخاذ المذكور في أنفسهم بعد بيان الصوارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the apparent reading, God did not show Iblis and his progeny the creation of the heavens and earth, which existed before them, or one another's creation.
rows.anchor: أي ما أحضرت إبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns refer to Iblis and his progeny, also called the misleaders; عضدا is a helper metaphor, and its indefinite form after negation excludes every kind of assistance.
rows.anchor: وهم المراد بالمضلين في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negation means God did not enlist them as assistants in creation or any divine affair, excluding even an imagined share in lordly governance.
rows.anchor: أي وما كنت متخذهم أعوانا في شأن الخلق

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islām keeps both pronouns tied to the devils to avoid splitting their reference and to preserve the apparent meaning of their selves.
rows.anchor: حذرا من تفكيك الضمير ومحافظة على ظاهر لفظ الأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also permits the second pronoun to refer to the human wrongdoers, accepting a split reference because denial that they witnessed the devils' creation invalidates their alliance.
rows.anchor: ولك أن ترجع الضمير الثاني إلى الظالمين ويلتزم التفكيك بناء على عود المعنى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion mocks the idolaters' poor reasoning: they need explicit explanation of an obvious point, and could not have witnessed creation unless God enabled it.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تهكم بالأفكار وإيذان بكمال ركاكة عقولهم وسخافة آرائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If heavens and earth includes their inhabitants, the verse denies that the devils witnessed the creation of the disbelievers themselves, avoiding a split between the pronouns.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد من السماوات والأرض ما يشمل أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes witnessing as consultation: God consulted no one in creating anyone, so the disbelievers have no basis for taking the devils as allies.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد به المشاورة مجازا وهو الذي يقتضيه ظاهر ما في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the consultation reading, denying assistance after denying consultation rules out any role for the devils, whether in judgment, opinion, or bringing things into being.
rows.anchor: ليؤدي الكلام ظاهرا عموم نفي مدخليتهم بوجه من الوجوه رأيا وإيجادا وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the second clause as denying that the devils created by their own wish or were created perfect; the poet's phrase خلق كما تشاء means created completely.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر خلقت مبرأ من كل عيب كأنك قد خلقت كما تشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that perfected beings literally witnessed their own fixed essences receive external existence is an implausible metaphysical interpretation.
rows.anchor: وزعم أن الكاملين شهدوا حقيقة خلق أنفسهم بمعنى أنهم رأوا وهم أعيان ثابتة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers both pronouns to refer to the nearby disbelievers who demanded that the poor be expelled; they did not govern creation, so their demand is baseless.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام بعد حكاية القول برجوع الضميرين إلى الشياطين الأقرب عندي عودهما على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to the disbelievers, they cannot know the world's primordial destiny and thus cannot claim honor and felicity for themselves and disgrace for the poor.
rows.anchor: جاهلون بما جرى به القلم في الأزل من أحوال السعادة وضدها لأنهم لم يكونوا شاهدين خلق العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the disbelievers were not shown creation's secrets or given unique qualities that would make them models for others; religion should not rely on their support.
rows.anchor: ما أطلعتهم على أسرار التكوين وما خصصتهم بخصائص لا يحويها غيرهم حتى يكونوا قدوة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, al-Jaḥdarī, al-Ḥasan, and Shayba read وما كنت with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, addressing the Prophet: it was not proper for him to seek their support.
rows.anchor: بفتح التاء خطابا له صلى الله عليه وسلم والمعنى ما صح لك الاعتضاد بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' request to expel poor believers aimed to drive people away from the Prophet; every misguided person also misleads through speech or conduct.
rows.anchor: لما أن قصدهم بطرد الفقراء تنفير الناس عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو إضلال ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to angels, the verse says they were not shown creation or enlisted as helpers, but were created to worship God; this account has a difficulty with calling them misleaders.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير ان للملائكة والمعنى ما أشهدتهم ذلك ولا استعنت بهم في شيء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the pronouns encompass the disbelievers and people generally, refuting astrologers, natural philosophers, physicians, and similar speculators.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية الضميران عائدان على الكفار وعلى الناس بالجملة فتتضمن الآية الرد على طوائف من المنجمين

rows.speaker: عبد الحق الصقلي
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq al-Ṣiqillī and some legal theorists also adopt the general reference to people who speculate about the world's governance.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب عبد الحق الصقلي وذكره بعض الأصوليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some jurists infer that non-Muslims should not be enlisted in religious matters such as fighting unbelievers or rebels; other jurists qualify the rule.
rows.anchor: واستدل بها على أنه لا ينبغي الاستعانة بالكافر وهو في أمور الدين كجهاد الكفار وقتال أهل البغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees no problem with non-Muslim help in worldly tasks, whether menial work or skilled construction and tailoring; he allows that ʿUmar's objection may concern religious work or reflect a stricter view.
rows.anchor: وأما الاستعانة بهم في أمور الدنيا فالذي يظهر أنه لا بأس بها سواء كانت في أمر ممتهن

rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: A Shiʿi account says ʿAlī refused Ibn ʿAbbās's advice to retain Muʿāwiya until his caliphate consolidated, citing the verse against taking a misleader as support; the author calls this a lie.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى الشيعة أن عليا كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال حين صمم على عزل معاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story attributing the verse to ʿAlī's removal of Muʿāwiya is fabricated and believed only by a misguided person.
rows.anchor: وهو كذب لا يعتقده إلا ضال مضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, al-Sakhtiyānī, ʿAwn al-ʿUqaylī, and Ibn Muqsam read ما أشهدناهم with the majestic first-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة والسختياني وعون العقيلي وابن مقسم / ما أشهدناهم / بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlī reads متخذا المضلين as an active participle in the accusative construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله وجهه / متخذا المضلين / على أعمال اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasan and ʿIkrima read عضدا with a silent ḍād and transferred vowel; ʿĪsā also uses a silent ḍād as a lightened Tamimi form, and has another reading with two fatḥas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعكرمة ﴿ عضدا ﴾ بسكون الضاد ونقل حركتها إلى العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayba and Abū ʿAmr, and also Ḥasan in reports, read عضدا with two ḍammas or two fatḥas; it may be a dialectal form or the plural of helper, removing the metaphor.
rows.anchor: وقرأ شيبة وأبو عمرو في رواية هرون وخارجة والخفاف وأبي زيد ﴿ عضدا ﴾ بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads عضدا with kasra on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the ḍād, a form the author does not find among its known dialects.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك ﴿ عضدا ﴾ بكسر العين وفتح الضاد ولم نجد ذلك من لغاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses the unbelievers, directly or through an intermediary, to rebuke and confound them, telling them to call their claimed partners for help or intercession.
rows.anchor: أي الله تعالى للكفار توبيخا وتعجيزا بواسطة أو بدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution of partners reflects their own claims that these beings were both partners and intercessors; the referents may be Iblis and his progeny or everything worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: والإضافة باعتبار ما كانوا يزعمون أيضا فإنهم كانوا يزعمون أنهم شركاء كما يزعمون أنهم شفعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the partners as Iblis and his progeny, whose substitution as allies follows from obeying their whisperings; another reading permits every object worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: وقد جوز غير واحد هنا أن يكون الكلام بتقدير زعمتموهم شركاء والمراد بهم إبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa, Yaḥyā, Ibn Abī Laylā, Ḥamza, and Ibn Muqsam read نقول with the majestic first-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة ويحيى وابن أبي ليلى وحمزة وابن مقسم ﴿ نقول ﴾ بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads شركاي with a shortened form attached to the first-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير / شركاي / مقصورا مضافا إلى الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on the partners demonstrates the idolaters' intense attempt to obtain intercession, though they cannot rescue them; spelling out their failure mocks their inability to grasp the obvious.
rows.anchor: وفيه بيان بكمال اعتنائهم بإغاثتهم على طريق الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موبق is a place of destruction derived from wabq, meaning to perish, and the callers and called beings share in that ruin, namely Hell.
rows.anchor: ﴿ موبقا ﴾ اسم مكان من وبق وبوقا كوثب وثوبا أو وبق وبقا كفرح فرحا إذا هلك

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Anas, and Mujāhid describe it as a valley in Hell flowing with blood and pus.
rows.anchor: وجاء عن ابن عمر وأنس ومجاهد أنه واد في جهنم يجري بدم وصديد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima describes a river of fire with dark, mule-sized serpents on its banks; when they surge toward the damned, they flee into the fire and call out.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه نهر في النار يسيل نارا على حافتيه حيات أمثال البغال الدهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain موبق as a place of destruction.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الموبق بالمهلك مروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وعن مجاهد وغيرهما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets it as enmity, the cause of destruction, comparing it with ʿUmar's saying that hatred can be destructive.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن تفسيره بالعداوة فهو مصدر أطلق على سبب الهلاك

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas interprets موبق as a prison.
rows.anchor: وعن الربيع بن أنس تفسيره بالمحبس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the destruction-place or prison is a barrier between the idolaters and their alleged partners, ending their hope of receiving intercession.
rows.anchor: معنى كون الموبق أي المهلك أو المحبس بينهم أنه حاجز واقع في البين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some who understand the word as a valley say God uses it to separate the people of guidance from the people of error, allowing the partners to include the honored figures mentioned by exegetes.
rows.anchor: وجاء عن بعض من فسره بالوادي أنه يفرق الله تعالى به بين أهل الهدى وأهل الضلالة

rows.speaker: الثعالبي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿālibī defines موبق as a distant barzakh; the great distance destroys their attempts to reach one another, and can separate Paradise's honored inhabitants from Hell's wicked ones.
rows.anchor: وقال الثعالبي في فقه اللغة الموبق بمعنى البرزخ البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If جعلنا means made or turned, بينهم is a complement and موبقا its first object; if it means created, بينهم is attached or describes the object, fronted for the verse ending.
rows.anchor: على جميع ما ذكر ظرف وهو مفعول ثان لجعل إن جعل بمعنى صير

rows.speaker: الفراء والسيرافي
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Sīrāfī take البين to mean connection rather than separation: God makes their worldly connection a cause of ruin on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء والسيرافي البين هنا بمعنى الوصل فانه يكون بمعناه كما يكون بمعنى الفراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit label criminals replaces a pronoun to condemn them for their wrongdoing; the sight of Hell is visual.
rows.anchor: وضع المظهر في مقام المضمر تصريحا بإجرامهم وذما لهم بذلك والرؤية بصرية

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that the Prophet said an unbeliever sees Hell from a journey of forty years away; al-Ḥākim graded the report sound.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري كما أخرجه عنه أحمد وابن جرير والحاكم وصححه عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses ظنوا as they knew; the author prefers this because the divine warning, failed pleas, and barrier make their entry certain.
rows.anchor: أي علموا كما أخرجه عبد الرزاق وجماعة عن قتادة وهو الظاهر من حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A literal reading of ظنوا means they only expected to enter Hell because they had not yet lost hope in God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل الظن على ظاهره وهم لم يتيقنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they saw Hell from afar and thought it would seize them immediately: entry itself was certain, but its timing was not.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم لما رأوها من بعيد كما سمعت في الحديث ظنوا أنهم تخطفهم في الحال

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The codex attributed to ʿAbd Allāh and readings by al-Aʿmash and Ibn Ghazwān from Ṭalḥa have ملاقوها, treated as an explanatory reading because it differs from the standard consonantal text.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قرأ الأعمش وابن غزوان عن طلحة واختير جعلها تفسيرا

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama reads ملافوها with a doubled fāʾ, from the idea of wrapping or enveloping something.
rows.anchor: بالفاء مشددة من لف الشيء

rows.speaker: أبو كبير الهذلي
rows.claim: مصرفا means a place to turn away to; Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī's poem witnesses it as a place noun, though a time noun is also possible.
rows.anchor: قال أبو كبير الهذلي أزهير هل عن شيبة بن مصرف أم لا خلود لباذل متكلف

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ and others allow مصرفا to be a verbal noun, but al-Durr al-Maṣūn calls this mistaken because its form with a kasra is not the ordinary verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المصور أنه سهو

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: The verbal-noun analysis is accepted for Zayd ibn ʿAlī's reading مصرفا with a fatḥa on the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: نعم أن القول بأنه مصدر مقبول في قراءة زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صرفنا means that God repeated the material and presented it in many forms of expression in the Qurʾān for people's benefit.
rows.anchor: كررنا وأوردنا على وجوه كثيرة من النظم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: On al-Akhfash's analysis, من is extra in من كل مثل and the phrase is the direct object of صرفنا.
rows.anchor: على أن من سيف خطيب على رأي الأخفش والمجرور مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, من is partitive and an omitted مثلا described by من كل مثل is the object, or the object is the content of the phrase, meaning examples from each needed category.
rows.anchor: أو مثلا من كل مثل على أن من أصلية والمفعول موصوف الجار والمجرور المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثل may mean familiar parables or striking qualities attractive to the soul; the point is that God varied useful examples that invite faith, not that He listed every possible parable.
rows.anchor: فالمراد من المثل إما معناه المشهور أو الصفة الغريبة التي هي في الحسن واستجلاب النفس كالمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that God provided these examples so people would accept faith, though they did not.
rows.anchor: وكأن في الآية حذفا أو هي على معنى ولقد فعلنا ذلك ليقبلوا فلم يفعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By its nature, the human being is exceptionally argumentative; in this context جدل means contentious, false disputation, while its root evokes twisting and bending one's opponent.
rows.anchor: وهو كما قال الراغب وغيره المنازعة بمفاوضة القول والأليق بالمقام أن يراد به هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جدلا is accusative as a specification: the human's arguing exceeds that of every other disputant; this is attributed to a volatile range between angelic heights and animal depths.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه على التمييز والمعنى أن جدل الإنسان أكثر من جدل كل مجادل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the argumentative human as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith or Ibn al-Zibʿarī; Ibn al-Sāʾib names Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who challenged resurrection with a crumbled bone.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به النضر بن الحرث وقيل ابن الزبعري وقال ابن السائب أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the general meaning of humanity, supported by the sound report that the Prophet applied the verse after ʿAlī's reply about their souls being in God's hand.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى ويؤيده ما أخرجه الشيخان وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن علي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports that when the Prophet urged him and Fāṭima to pray at night, he answered that God held their souls and would raise them if He wished; the Prophet struck his thigh and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: إنما أنفسنا بيد الله تعالى إن شاء أن يبعثنا بعثنا فانصرف حين قلت ذلك

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī says the Prophet struck his thigh from amazement at the quick answer and its refusal to accept his exhortation as an excuse; another view treats the Prophet as accepting their excuse.
rows.anchor: حيث قال المختار في معناه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم تعجب من سرعة جوابه وعدم موافقته له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the report clearly supports a general reading but says it raises an unresolved difficulty that reflection does not remove.
rows.anchor: إلا أن فيه إشكالا يعرف بالتأمل ولا يدفعه ما ذكره النووي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others identify the people as Quraysh's unbelievers, whose false claims were just recounted; ما is negative, though an unusual opinion makes it interrogative.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية وغيره المراد بهم كفار قريش الذين حكيت أباطيلهم وما نافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance can mean the Qurʾān or the Messenger, with the designation guidance intensifying the description of either.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن العظيم الهادي إلى الإيمان بما فيه من فنون المعاني الموجبة له أو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness means repenting of all prior sins, including false argument; mentioning it after faith broadens the demand, though the author rejects the claim that faith alone cannot erase prior sins.
rows.anchor: بالتوبة عما فرط منهم من أنواع الذنوب التي من جملتها مجادلتهم الحق بالباطل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says faith joined to seeking forgiveness is more complete, so both are mentioned to require the fullest state; the author calls this unconvincing.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن الإيمان مع الاستغفار أكمل من الإيمان وحده

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation says forgiveness follows faith to clarify that genuine faith without hypocrisy is intended.
rows.anchor: لتأكيد أن المراد منه الإيمان الذي لا يشوبه نفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first coming exception is the destructive precedent God enacted among earlier nations, specifically annihilating punishment; the possessive is theirs because it befell them.
rows.anchor: وهم من أهلك من الأمم السابقة وإضافة السنة إليهم قيل لكونها جارية عليهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies an omitted genitive: what prevented them was seeking destruction in this life, since actual destruction would excuse them from faith.
rows.anchor: قاله الزجاج وجوز صاحب الفينان تقدير انتظار أي ما منعهم إلا انتظار الهلاك

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī supplies God's decree that destruction come upon them and says the verse concerns those killed at Badr and Uḥud, though the Meccan setting weighs against this.
rows.anchor: وقدر الواحدي تقدير أي ما منعهم إلا تقدير الله تعالى اتيان الهلاك عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted-word readings avoid making punishment itself an excuse for failing to believe; the afterlife punishment in the next clause is certainly awaited, and its timing follows the opportunity for faith.
rows.anchor: والداعي لتقدير المضاف أنه لو كان المانع من إيمانهم واستغفارهم نفس إتيان الهلاك كانوا معذورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that asking for destruction follows their disbelief, so treating the request as what prevents faith makes the argument circular; the proposed reply identifies the request's cause as obstinacy.
rows.anchor: واعترض تقدير الطلب بأن طلبهم سنة الأولين لعدم إيمانهم وهو لمنعهم عن الإيمان فلو كان منعهم للطلب لزوم الدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their obstinacy is illustrated by the demand in Qurʾān 8:32 for stones to fall if the message is true; the objection remains that some disbelievers deny the truth without being obstinate.
rows.anchor: بمثل قولهم ( اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء ) الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection says disbelief precedes and continues beyond the verbal request; the reply distinguishes prior unbelief from the later failure to change, but the author finds this weak.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن المتقدم على الطلب هو عدم الإيمان السابق وليس الطلب بمانع منه بل هو مانع مما تحقق بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the request as merely verbal: no sensible person inwardly seeks doom, so their words expose their denial of the Prophet's warning; the author still finds difficulty in it.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد من الطلب الطلب الصوري اللساني لا الحقيقي القلبي فإن من له أدنى عقل لا يطلب الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view reads the request idiomatically as deserving punishment; an objection is that unbelief causes that desert, so the supposed barrier would come after the cause.
rows.anchor: الطلب الطلب بلسان الاستعداد وأن مآل الآية ما منعهم من ذلك إلا استعداداتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author locates the real cause in their bad preparedness and nature, which produce both unbelief and liability; their disposition itself seeks the opposite of faith and thus the destruction following it.
rows.anchor: السبب الحقيقي سوء استعداداتهم وخباثة ماهياتهم في نفس الأمر وهذا كما أنه سبب للاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People might plead that no messenger came and that heedlessness kept them from faith, but this is not a stronger excuse; their bad disposition cannot serve as a conscious plea.
rows.anchor: أن الكفار لو لم يأتهم رسول ينبههم من سنة الغفلة يحتجون لو عذبوا بعدم إتيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can preserve the apparent idea that only their request for foretold destruction remained after the Messenger's guidance, while that request could not count as a valid excuse or obstacle.
rows.anchor: لا مانع لهم من أن يؤمنوا أو يستغفروا ربهم ولا حجة بعد مجيء الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After allowing for the objections, the author prefers تقدير as the barrier; those who explain it through preparedness treat preparedness as its source, while al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām identifies God's will.
rows.anchor: والأولى تقدير التقدير وهو مانع بلا شبهة إلا أن القائلين بالاستعداد حسبما تعلم يجعلون منشأه الاستعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two Qurʾānic exclusions are reconciled by taking this verse to name the real barrier, God's will, and 17:94 to name the customary barrier, surprise that a human could be a messenger.
rows.anchor: ودفع التنافي بين الحصر المستفاد من هذه الآية والحصر المستفاد من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says there are several barriers: divine knowledge of their unbelief is incompatible with faith, and the motive for unbelief also prevents faith; the verse may deny only perceptible obstacles.
rows.anchor: وادعى الإمام تعدد الموانع وأن المراد من الآية فقدان نوع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قبلا with two ḍammas may be the plural of قبيل, meaning kinds of punishment, or may mean visibly and face-to-face, as Abū ʿUbayda reports.
rows.anchor: والقبل بضمتين جمع قبيل وهو النوع أي أو يأتيهم العذاب أنواعا وألوانا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says قبلا may mean face-to-face and derives that sense from confrontation; it can modify the people or the punishment as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: فإن أبا عبيدة حكاهما معا بهذا المعنى وأصله بمعنى المقابلة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة والزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Zamakhsharī report قبلا with two fatḥas meaning facing or forthcoming.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن قتيبة والزمخشري أنه قريء ( قبلا ) بفتحتين أي مستقبلا

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Ghazwān from Ṭalḥa read قبيلا, meaning visibly and face-to-face.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وابن غزوان عن طلحة ( قبيلا ) بقاف مفتوحة وباء مكسورة بعدها ياء ساكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers are sent only to bring believers good news of reward and warn unbelievers and sinners of punishment, not to satisfy demands for signs after miracles or be treated improperly.
rows.anchor: ﴿ مبشرين ﴾ للمؤمنين بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers argue falsely by demanding further signs, asking about the Companions of the Cave, and claiming the Prophet seeks superiority or should be an angel.
rows.anchor: اقتراح ذلك والسؤال عن قصة أصحاب الكهف ونحوها تعنتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction to false disputation marks the censured kind of argument, while جدل in ordinary language is broader; يدحضوا means to remove or invalidate the truth.
rows.anchor: وتقييد الجدال بالباطل لبيان المذموم منه فإنه كما مر غير بعيد عام لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of يدحضوا evokes slipping on mud; two poetic lines support the usage, and the image may transfer a physical slippery surface to argument or liken their words to mire.
rows.anchor: والدحض الطين الذي يزلق فيه قال الشاعر : وردت ونجى اليشكري حذاره

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī compares their arguments to mire that makes the proofs of guidance slip.
rows.anchor: كقول الخفاجي : أتانا بوحل لأفكاره ليزلق أقدام هدى الحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs include the statements or deeds supporting the messengers; what they were warned against can mean the threatening calamities or the warning itself, and هزوا means mockery.
rows.anchor: التي أيدت بها الرسل سواء كانت قولا أو فعلا ( وما أنذروا ( أي والذي أنذروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads هزأ with a silent hamza; the other canonical readers except Ḥafṣ read it with two ḍammas, as an intensive verbal noun used adjectivally or meaning something mocked.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ( هزأ ) بالسكون مهموزا وقرأ غيره وغير حفص من السبعة بضمتين مهموزا

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most exegetes take God's signs as the Qurʾān, supported by the following phrase about understanding it; the reference may also include all signs, with the Qurʾān foremost.
rows.anchor: الأكثرون على أن المراد بها القرآن العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies that anyone equals the person who is reminded of God's signs and turns away without reflection or admonition; their disputation and mockery are extreme wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وحقق غير واحد أن المراد نفي أن يساوي أحد في الظلم من وعظ بآيات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting what one's hands sent ahead means failing to reflect on the consequences of one's unbelief, sins, false disputes, and mockery of truth.
rows.anchor: أي عمله من الكفر والمعاصي التي من جملتها المجادلة بالباطل والاستهزاء بالحق

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the people meant as the polytheists of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والمراد ( ممن ) عند الأكثرين مشركوا مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description may apply to anyone with these traits, with Meccan polytheists included first; the plural pronoun then refers to them collectively.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد منه المتصف بما في حيز الصلة كائنا من كان ويدخل فيه مشركو مكة دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory answer says their turning away and forgetfulness result from coverings over their hearts and heaviness in their ears; أكنة is plural of cover, with the tanwin possibly indicating abundance.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل ما علة الإعراض والنسيان فقيل علته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in أن يفقهوه may refer to the signs in their intended sense, the Qurʾān directly, or an omitted purpose: aversion to understanding it or prevention of beneficial understanding.
rows.anchor: الضمير المنصوب عند الأكثرين للآيات وتذكيره وإفراده باعتبار المعنى المراد منها وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ears contain a heaviness that prevents meaningful hearing; if the Prophet calls them to guidance, they will never find it throughout the period of moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: وفي ءاذانهم ( أي وجعلنا فيه ( وقرا ( ثقلا أن يسمعوه سماعا كذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads إذن as a consequential answer: if the Prophet were to call them, their established state would make the call produce the opposite of guidance; he is imagined as asking why he should not invite them.
rows.anchor: و ( إذن ) جزاء وجواب كما حقق المراد منه في موضعه

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf explains that إذن explicitly signals the hypothetical consequence, and the Prophet is cast as a questioner to emphasize that their sealed hearts prevent response.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى إذن لو دعوت وهو من التعكيس بلا تعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absolute warning concerns Meccan polytheists whom God knew would remain unbelievers when the verse came; later conversions by some do not contradict the specific foretelling.
rows.anchor: والآية في أناس علم الله تعالى موافاتهم على الكفر من مشركي مكة حين نزولها

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī notes that determinists use this verse while proponents of human choice use the preceding verse; the Qurʾān often places evidence for both sides together as a test of understanding.
rows.anchor: واستدلت الجبرية بهذه الآية على مذهبهم والقدرية بالآية التي قبلها قال الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربك الغفور is subject and predicate, with ذو الرحمة as a second predicate of the subject.
rows.anchor: ( وربك الغفور ) مبتدأ وخبر وقوله تعالى ( ذو الرحمة (

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the intensive form الغفور is used because forgiveness is withholding harm, which can extend across limitless harms, whereas bringing infinitely many benefits is impossible.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر لفظ المبالغة في المغفرة دون الرحمة لأن المغفرة ترك الأضرار والرحمة إيصال النفع

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Naysābūrī objects that ذو الرحمة also conveys intensity, that the Qurʾān often intensifies both forgiveness and mercy, and that God's capacities are finite without a difference between omission and action.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه النيسابوري بأنه فرق دقيق لو ساعده النقل على أن قوله تعالى ( ذو الرحمة ) لا يخلو عن مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says a surface reading that God's capacities are finite sounds like incapacity, but interprets the statement charitably and asks the reader to reflect.
rows.anchor: لقد قف شعري من ظاهر قول النيسابوري أن مقدوراته تعالى متناهية فإن ظاهره التعجيز

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A defense says غفار means willing to remove punishment from the deserving and رحيم willing to bestow benefits; intensity in one context does not preclude it elsewhere, and created outcomes are finite though divine possibilities are not.
rows.anchor: إنهم فسروا الغفار بمريد إزالة العقوبة عن مستحقها والرحيم بمريد الأنعام على الخلق

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers claim that what enters existence among God's possible acts is also infinite, since they reject the proof by successive comparison when its requirements of coexistence and order are absent.
rows.anchor: وزعمت الفلاسفة أن ما دخل في الوجود من المقدورات غير متناه أيضا ولا يجري فيه برهان التطبيق عندهم

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī explains the contrast contextually: after withholding immediate punishment for grave sins, God displays great forgiveness and mercy, yet does not grant the ultimate mercy that would save them altogether.
rows.anchor: أن المذكور بعد عدم مؤاخذتهم بما كسبوا من الجرم العظيم وهو مغفرة عظيمة وترك التعجيل رحمة منه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A defense of al-Rāzī's distinction says withholding all possible kinds of immediate punishment can be unlimited in a way that positive mercy need not be; the author notes a difficulty in the argument.
rows.anchor: لأن الترك عدمي يجوز فيه عدم التناهي بخلاف الآخر ألا ترى أن ترك عذابهم دال على ترك جميع أنواع العقوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذو الرحمة may itself intensify the attribute through the definite article, or through ذو, whose construction conveys stronger possession than a simple adjective.
rows.anchor: إن ذلك إما لاقتران الرحمة بأل فتفيد الرحمة الكاملة أو الرحمة المعهودة التي وسعت كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذو الرحمة may be more emphatic than either الرحمن or الرحيم because it is unqualified by this-worldly or otherworldly mercy; together those two names can still exceed it, as in the basmala.
rows.anchor: ولذا عدل عنهما إلى ذو الرحمة وإذا قلت هما مثله في عدم التقييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction ذو العلم conveys fuller possession of knowledge than عالم or العليم, and mercy covers a wider range than forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ومن أنصف لم يشك في أن قولك فلان ذو العلم أبلغ من قولك فلان عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis on mercy comforts the Prophet after telling him that some people are sealed against guidance despite his intense concern; addressing him as Lord's own servant deepens the reassurance.
rows.anchor: والنكتة فيه ههنا مزيد إيناسه صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد أن أخبره سبحانه بالطبع على قلوب بعض المرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness comes first because cleansing precedes adornment, or because it is more relevant to the context of delaying punishment despite their deserving it.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم الوصف الأول لأن التخلية قبل التحلية أو لأنه أهم بحسب الحال والمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لو يؤاخذهم means if God willed to take them to account for what they did; ما may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun covering their sins, including disputation and turning away.
rows.anchor: أي لو يريد مؤاخذتهم ﴿ بما كسبوا ﴾ أي فعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording مؤاخذة suggests a severe, swift taking to task; the present tense placed where a past is meant signals God's continuing non-willingness to hasten punishment.
rows.anchor: وإيثار صيغة الاستقبال وإن كان المعنى على المضي لإفادة أن انتفاء تعجيل العذاب لهم بسبب استمرار عدم إرادة المؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The موعد may be the day of Badr or Resurrection as a time, or Hell as a place; the clause contrasts a fixed appointment with immediate seizure.
rows.anchor: وهو يوم بدر أو يوم القيامة على أن الموعد اسم زمان وجوز أن يكون اسم مكان والمراد منه جهنم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses موئلا as a means of escape and cites the poet al-Aʿshā's use of the root for being saved.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء أي منجا يقال وألت نفس فلان نجت وعليه قوله الأعشى

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes موئل as a refuge; Mujāhid says a protected place and al-Ḍaḥḥāk a way out, with the author considering the distinction minor.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة هو الملجأ يقال وأل فلان إلى كذا يئل وألا ووؤولا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The refuge interpretation is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās; موئل may be a time or place noun, with its pronoun apparently referring to the appointment.
rows.anchor: وتفسيره بالملجأ مروي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A less apparent reading makes the pronoun refer to the punishment itself, intensifying the threat because the punishment would be their only refuge and no escape would remain.
rows.anchor: وقيل على العذاب وفيه من المبالغة ما فيه لدلالته على أنهم لا خلاص لهم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading that makes من دونه refer to God is against the apparent antecedent and adds no rhetorical force.
rows.anchor: وقيل يعود على الله تعالى وهو مخالف للظاهر مع الخلو عن المبالغة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads مولا with a doubled wāw, without hamza or yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري مولا بتشديد الواو من غير همز ولا ياء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, through al-Ḥalwānī from al-Zuhrī, reads مولا with a light wāw and kasra, also without hamza or yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر عن الحلواني عنه مولا بكسر الواو خفيفة من غير همز ولا ياء
